distinct-operations-need-tools-01.graded_text: Agents can search page content across the workspace in one call, through a dedicated search tool or a content query on a listing tool, with explicit scope and pagination, instead of reading pages one by one. The query uses familiar text-search semantics (plain text, phrase, or regular expression) rather than a bespoke query language.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:10: "`search_pages` | `{ query, folder?, cursor?, limit? }` | Read-only. Finds pages whose title or Markdown contains `query` as a case-insensitive literal phrase, searching the whole workspace or one folder and its subfolders. ... Default 20 per page, maximum 50." One call across the workspace, explicit folder scope, cursor/limit paging, and plain literal-phrase matching rather than a bespoke query language.

distinct-operations-need-tools-02.graded_text: Placing a print order is its own tool, not a file write, a special path, or a flag on an existing tool, because it charges money and ships goods.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:11: "`order_prints` | `{ paths[], copies, ship_to, idempotency_key }` | Orders `copies` printed, bound copies of the listed pages ... charges the workspace's card on file, and ships to `ship_to`". This is a dedicated tool. write_page, edit_page and delete_pages rows (lines 7-9) are unchanged and carry no print flag or path.

distinct-operations-need-tools-03.graded_text: A retried print-order call after a timeout cannot charge twice: the design states an idempotency key, a single-use quote or order ID, or an equivalent server-side guard.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:11: "Use a new `idempotency_key` for each new order: a repeated call with the same key never charges or ships again and returns the first call's order, so after a timeout, retry with the same key." idempotency_key is a required argument (no `?`).

distinct-operations-need-tools-04.graded_text: The catalog adds no generic execute, run, or action tool.
